parole.testo: From Huron / Wyandot ondatra or ondathra, attested in Gabriel Sagard's 1632 French Dictionnaire de la langue huronne and found in the Huron dialects of the Hochelaga region of Canada.

parole.significato: A mystical power thought by the Iroquois to pervade all things.
parole.testo: Supposedly coined in 1902 by American ethnologist John Napoleon Brinton Hewitt using a Wyandot (Iroquoian) cognate to Mohawk orę́·naʔ (“inherent power”).

parole.significato: A member of a Native American people, formed from the Huron confederacy, that lived in and around Ohio.
A member of the Wyandotte people.
A greeting, used in representations of Native American speech.
parole.testo: From a Siouan language; compare Lakota háu. Alternatively from Wyandot haau.

parole.motivo_incerta: Uncertain; Possibly; or from; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: A member of the Wyandot people, a Native American group.
parole.testo: From French Huron; Uncertain; possibly from French hure (“boar’s head”) or from a Wyandot word containing the Iroquoian root ronon (“nation”), from Proto-North Iroquoian *-ɹonõʔ.
